q: Which property holds for every node of a binary search tree?
opts: Keys in the left sub tree are smaller and keys in the right sub tree are larger
Keys in the left sub tree are larger and keys in the right sub tree are smaller
Both sub tree always have the same height
All keys in the tree are equal
ansText: Keys in the left sub tree are smaller and keys in the right sub tree are larger
expl: The BST rule holds at EVERY node, which is why inorder traversal automatically gives sorted order.

q: Which traversal of a binary search tree visits the keys in ascending order?
expl: Inorder = left, root, right -> for a BST this is exactly the sorted order. (Preorder/postorder give useful but unsorted orders.)

q: What is the maximum number of children a node can have in a binary tree?
expl: Binary = at most two children (left and right). A node may have 0, 1 or 2 children.

q: If the root is at height 0, what is the maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height h?
expl: Level i can hold 2^i nodes; levels 0..h sum to 1 + 2 + 4 + ... + 2^h = 2^(h+1) - 1. Example: height 2 -> up to 7 nodes.

q: A tree with n nodes has how many edges?
expl: Every node except the root has exactly one incoming edge, so n nodes give n - 1 edges.

q: Which operations are used to restore the red-black properties after an insertion?
expl: After inserting a red node, the tree fixes red-red conflicts by recolouring and, when needed, rotating - never by deleting or re-sorting.

q: Which property is true for a red-black tree?
opts: A red node cannot have a red child
ansText: A red node cannot have a red child
expl: The red rule forbids two consecutive red nodes on a path. The root is always BLACK (B is a trap), and leaves are considered black.

q: What do the internal nodes of an expression tree contain?
expl: Leaves hold operands (numbers/variables); internal nodes hold the operators (+, -, *, /) that combine their subtrees.

q: What is the colour of the root node in a red-black tree?
expl: The root must be black - this is checked explicitly in the red-black colouring program (color[0] == 'R' means invalid).

q: Where is the largest key located in a binary search tree?
expl: Keep going right from the root until there is no right child (findMax walks temp->right). The leftmost node holds the minimum.

q: Which rotation corrects the Left-Right (LR) imbalance in an AVL tree?
opts: Right rotation followed by left rotation
Left rotation followed by right rotation
ansText: Left rotation followed by right rotation
expl: LR case: the left child leans right, so first rotate LEFT around the left child, then rotate RIGHT around the root. (C describes the RL case - read the letters carefully.)

q: Which balance factor values are allowed for every node of an AVL tree?
expl: Balance factor = height(left) - height(right) must stay in {-1, 0, +1}. If it becomes ±2, a rotation is required immediately.

q: In a trie, what does the path from the root to a node represent?
opts: A prefix of one or more stored strings
The balance factor of the node
ansText: A prefix of one or more stored strings
expl: Every root-to-node path spells the leading characters shared by words, e.g. the path r-a in 'rat/ram' is the prefix 'ra'.

q: Which of the following is a common application of a trie?
opts: Finding shortest paths in a graph
expl: Tries answer 'how many words start with this prefix?' by walking down the tree - exactly the search-box suggestion program in this unit.
